paras.text: In this unit, we will turn our attention to environmental issues, associated with Earth’s atmosphere. Air and water pollutions are the major problems in most of the World’s cities. The atmosphere, a part of the environment, acts as repository for emissions from combustion and from many other human activities. The air can be cleansed by natural mechanisms but these can be overwhelmed by the amount of pollutants being produced. Human activities are increasing the atmospheric concentration of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases. In addition, the stratospheric ozone shield, which protects us from the ultraviolet rays, is threatened by the emission of ozone-destroying chemicals.

The quality of surface and ground water is of concern due to two distinct points of view, that is, human health and welfare and the health of aquatic ecosystems.

The atmosphere absorbs most of the cosmic rays from the outer space and harmful radiation such as U.V. through ozone (O₃) layer. paras.text: Troposphere is the part we live in. It extends from the surface of the Earth up to 11 kilo meters. It constitutes about 10% of the atmosphere’s height but contains 80% of its mass. The temperature in this sphere ranges from 15°C to –56°C (Table 23.1). Nearly all atmosphere water vapours is found in the troposphere so it is the layer where most of the Earth’s weather phenomena occurs. The important chemicals that exist in this sphere are N₂, O₂, CO₂ and H₂O(vapours). It is also a region of much turbulence, due to the global energy flow that results from the imbalances of heating and cooling rates between the equator and the poles. The temperature in troposphere falls off uniformly with increase in altitude. Thus, the air it contains is mixed rapidly by convection.

sections.theory:
Introduction

In this unit, we will turn our attention to environmental issues, associated with Earth’s atmosphere. Air and water pollutions are the major problems in most of the World’s cities. The atmosphere, a part of the environment, acts as repository for emissions from combustion and from many other human activities. The air can be cleansed by natural mechanisms but these can be overwhelmed by the amount of pollutants being produced. Human activities are increasing the atmospheric concentration of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases. In addition, the stratospheric ozone shield, which protects us from the ultraviolet rays, is threatened by the emission of ozone-destroying chemicals.

Likewise, water quality is an important issue. Although most of the water supply is returned to the stream flow after use, its quality is necessarily degraded. The quality of surface and ground water is of concern due to two distinct points of view, that is, human health and welfare and the health of aquatic ecosystems.

Atmosphere is the envelop of gases, surrounding the Earth’s surface. It plays a key role to sustain life on Earth and save it from the hazardous environment of the outer space. The atmosphere absorbs most of the cosmic rays from the outer space and harmful radiation such as U.V. through ozone (O₃) layer. In addition, the atmosphere maintains the heat balance of the earth through absorption of energy from the sun and re-emitted.

The atmosphere can be divided into different layers based on their temperature and characteristics. Starting from the surface of the Earth, going vertically upwards, these layers or regions are as follows:

i. Troposphere   ii. Stratosphere   iii. Mesosphere   iv. Thermosphere   v. Exosphere

Table: 23.1 The Regions of Atmosphere

23.1 Chemistry of the Troposphere

Troposphere is the part we live in. It extends from the surface of the Earth up to 11 kilo meters. It constitutes about 10% of the atmosphere’s height but contains 80% of its mass. The temperature in this sphere ranges from 15°C to –56°C (Table 23.1). Nearly all atmosphere water vapours is found in the troposphere so it is the layer where most of the Earth’s weather phenomena occurs. The important chemicals that exist in this sphere are N₂, O₂, CO₂ and H₂O(vapours). It is also a region of much turbulence, due to the global energy flow that results from the imbalances of heating and cooling rates between the equator and the poles. The temperature in troposphere falls off uniformly with increase in altitude. Thus, the air it contains is mixed rapidly by convection.

23.1.1 Chemical Reactions in the Atmosphere

Apart from the chemicals mentioned earlier, in some areas (particularly the industries zones), the atmosphere (troposphere) may also contain SOₓ and NOₓ gases which are responsible for the acid rain. For example, NO₂ or SO₂ react with oxygen in the presence of rain water and produce acids.

The concentration of the acid thus formed can be quite higher, which ultimately reduces the pH of rain water substantially. This results in producing, what is called, acid rain. The CO₂ present in the atmosphere (0.036%) also reacts with the rain water, making it slightly acidic (pH ≅ 5.6).

پہلے بیان کردہ کیمیکلز کے علاوہ بعض علاقوں (خاص طور پر صنعتی علاقوں) میں فضا (ٹروپوسفیئر) میں SOₓ اور NOₓ گیسیں بھی ہو سکتی ہیں جو تیزابی بارش کی ذمہ دار ہیں۔ مثلاً NO₂ یا SO₂ بارش کے پانی کی موجودگی میں آکسیجن سے تعامل کر کے تیزاب بناتے ہیں۔

اس طرح بننے والے تیزاب کا ارتکاز کافی زیادہ ہو سکتا ہے جو بالآخر بارش کے پانی کا pH کافی کم کر دیتا ہے۔ اس کے نتیجے میں وہ بنتی ہے جسے تیزابی بارش کہتے ہیں۔ فضا میں موجود CO₂ (0.036%) بھی بارش کے پانی سے تعامل کر کے اسے ہلکا تیزابی (pH ≅ 5.6) بنا دیتی ہے۔

اس یونٹ میں ہم زمین کی فضا سے وابستہ ماحولیاتی مسائل پر توجہ دیں گے۔ ہوا اور پانی کی آلودگی دنیا کے زیادہ تر شہروں کے بڑے مسائل ہیں۔ فضا، جو ماحول کا ایک حصہ ہے، احتراق اور دوسری بہت سی انسانی سرگرمیوں کے اخراجات کے لیے ذخیرہ گاہ کا کام کرتی ہے۔ ہوا قدرتی طریقوں سے صاف ہو سکتی ہے لیکن پیدا ہونے والی آلودگیوں کی مقدار ان پر غالب آ سکتی ہے۔ انسانی سرگرمیاں فضا میں کاربن ڈائی آکسائیڈ اور دوسری گرین ہاؤس گیسوں کا ارتکاز بڑھا رہی ہیں۔ مزید یہ کہ سٹریٹوسفیئر کی اوزون ڈھال، جو ہمیں بالائے بنفشی شعاعوں سے بچاتی ہے، اوزون تباہ کرنے والے کیمیکلز کے اخراج سے خطرے میں ہے۔

له مخکې یاد شویو کیمیکلونو سربېره، په ځینو سیمو (په ځانګړي ډول صنعتي سیمو) کې اتموسفیر (ټروپوسفیر) کېدای شي SOₓ او NOₓ ګازونه هم ولري چې د تېزابي باران مسؤل دي. د بېلګې په توګه NO₂ یا SO₂ د باران د اوبو په شتون کې له اکسیجن سره تعامل کوي او اسیدونه تولیدوي.

په دې ډول د جوړ شوي اسید غلظت کېدای شي ډېر لوړ وي چې په پای کې د باران د اوبو pH په ډېره کچه ټیټوي. په پایله کې هغه څه جوړېږي چې تېزابي باران بلل کېږي. په اتموسفیر کې شته CO₂ (0.036%) هم د باران له اوبو سره تعامل کوي او هغه لږ تېزابي (pH ≅ 5.6) کوي.
sections.content:
Introduction

In this unit, we will turn our attention to environmental issues, associated with Earth’s atmosphere. Air and water pollutions are the major problems in most of the World’s cities. The atmosphere, a part of the environment, acts as repository for emissions from combustion and from many other human activities. The air can be cleansed by natural mechanisms but these can be overwhelmed by the amount of pollutants being produced. Human activities are increasing the atmospheric concentration of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases. In addition, the stratospheric ozone shield, which protects us from the ultraviolet rays, is threatened by the emission of ozone-destroying chemicals.

Likewise, water quality is an important issue. Although most of the water supply is returned to the stream flow after use, its quality is necessarily degraded. The quality of surface and ground water is of concern due to two distinct points of view, that is, human health and welfare and the health of aquatic ecosystems.

Atmosphere is the envelop of gases, surrounding the Earth’s surface. It plays a key role to sustain life on Earth and save it from the hazardous environment of the outer space. The atmosphere absorbs most of the cosmic rays from the outer space and harmful radiation such as U.V. through ozone (O₃) layer. In addition, the atmosphere maintains the heat balance of the earth through absorption of energy from the sun and re-emitted.

The atmosphere can be divided into different layers based on their temperature and characteristics. Starting from the surface of the Earth, going vertically upwards, these layers or regions are as follows:

i. Troposphere ii. Stratosphere iii. Mesosphere iv. Thermosphere v. Exosphere

Table: 23.1 The Regions of Atmosphere

23.1 Chemistry of the Troposphere

Troposphere is the part we live in. It extends from the surface of the Earth up to 11 kilo meters. It constitutes about 10% of the atmosphere’s height but contains 80% of its mass. The temperature in this sphere ranges from 15°C to –56°C (Table 23.1). Nearly all atmosphere water vapours is found in the troposphere so it is the layer where most of the Earth’s weather phenomena occurs. The important chemicals that exist in this sphere are N₂, O₂, CO₂ and H₂O(vapours). It is also a region of much turbulence, due to the global energy flow that results from the imbalances of heating and cooling rates between the equator and the poles. The temperature in troposphere falls off uniformly with increase in altitude. Thus, the air it contains is mixed rapidly by convection.

23.1.1 Chemical Reactions in the Atmosphere

Apart from the chemicals mentioned earlier, in some areas (particularly the industries zones), the atmosphere (troposphere) may also contain SOₓ and NOₓ gases which are responsible for the acid rain. For example, NO₂ or SO₂ react with oxygen in the presence of rain water and produce acids.

The concentration of the acid thus formed can be quite higher, which ultimately reduces the pH of rain water substantially. This results in producing, what is called, acid rain. The CO₂ present in the atmosphere (0.036%) also reacts with the rain water, making it slightly acidic (pH ≅ 5.6).
